title: National Gallery of Victoria: Masterpieces
subtitle: From a broad river valley to a handful of coins, twenty works show how size and distance organise a picture.
introduction:
Streeton's river bends through a view too broad for any one small incident to control. In Tucker's *Judas*, a cramped body, a wooden form and coins occupy almost all the available attention. Between those extremes, a garden can become a working place, a portrait can depend on the relative sizes of hands and head, and a battle can set an ordered formation against individual danger.

Scale here means more than a canvas's dimensions. It includes what a painter brings close, reduces, enlarges or leaves without a familiar measure. This selection follows those decisions across landscape, portraiture and narrative, ending with colour areas that offer no object against which to judge their extent.
visitNote: The NGV displays its Australian and international collections at separate sites. Check each work's collection page and the current information for NGV International and the Ian Potter Centre.

books.title: The Elements of Drawing
books.author: John Ruskin
books.note: The Elements of Drawing asks readers to study the structure of trees, clouds and shadows closely. It supplies practical questions for looking at Southern, Sutherland and Streeton, without pretending to describe their intentions.

works.title: The Purple Noon's Transparent Might
works.credit: Arthur Streeton. The purple noon’s transparent might. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Full source frame, proportional resize and JPEG compression. https://www.wikiart.org/en/arthur-streeton/the-purple-noon-s-transparent-might-1896
works.description: Seen from above, the river gives the broad view a continuous bend to follow. Its nearer blue remains strong while distant hills and sky lose contrast. Streeton makes the apparent heat a relation between distances, rather than an added anecdote about the day. The changing clarity of the land carries the sensation across the whole prospect.

works.title: The House at Rueil
works.credit: Édouard Manet. The House at Rueil. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The trunk interrupts the façade near its centre, preventing a complete architectural presentation. Pale walls and blue shutters remain readable through separate patches between tree and garden growth. Manet lets the obstruction organise attention instead of clearing it away. The house is encountered as something seen from a particular garden position, with parts necessarily withheld.

works.title: Boulevard Montmartre, Morning, Grey Weather
works.credit: Camille Pissarro. Boulevard Montmartre Morning, Grey Weather. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Repeated marks turn pedestrians and carriages into a collective movement along the narrowing street. Buildings and bare trees supply the larger recession, while the grey distance reduces individual definition. Pissarro allows the city's traffic to remain many events at once. A figure need not acquire a separate story to contribute to the visible life of the boulevard.

works.title: Lion Attacking a Horse
works.credit: George Stubbs. Lion Attacking a Horse. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The animals lock into a single struggle above the low landscape. The horse's stretched neck extends the effect of the lion's grip through its whole body. Stubbs uses anatomical articulation to make force understandable: the attack is registered by the victim's twisting response. Pale and dark masses distinguish the participants even where their positions become inseparable.

works.title: Antaeus Setting Down Dante and Virgil
works.catalogueTitle: Antaeus setting down Dante and Virgil in the last circle of hell
works.credit: William Blake. Antaeus setting down Dante and Virgil in the last circle of hell. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The giant's bent body becomes the means by which the smaller poets move through the scene. Blake makes scale perform the narrative: a single figure can bridge a distance that would otherwise require a landscape route. Following his curve takes the eye toward the depths below, joining the act of looking to the act of being lowered.

works.title: Portrait of the Painter Manuel Humbert
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of the painter Manuel Humbert
works.credit: Amedeo Modigliani. Portrait of the painter Manuel Humbert. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/amedeo-modigliani/portrait-of-the-painter-manuel-humbert-1916-1
works.description: Small warm hands counter the elongated head and neck above the dark suit. Modigliani changes bodily proportion without making posture irrelevant. The frontal presentation remains a seated person's arrangement, with compact gestures below and a stretched facial form above. The portrait's balance depends on keeping those unequal scales in relation rather than correcting them into anatomical uniformity.

works.title: An Old Bee Farm
works.credit: Clara Southern. An Old Bee Farm. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Hives identify the clearing as a place of work, but they remain embedded in grass and cool light. The figure's activity occupies one part of a setting that includes weathered objects and a small building. Southern gives the whole modest environment sustained attention. Human use is present without requiring a worker to dominate every other element.

works.title: Evensong
works.credit: Clara Southern. Evensong. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Violet and grey draw houses, sloping ground and valley into a narrowing tonal range. Evening is established across the view rather than announced by a spectacular sun. Southern makes reduced differences do the work of time. The landscape stays locatable while its parts begin to share the conditions of fading light.

works.title: Field Naturalists
works.credit: Jane Sutherland. Field Naturalists. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The people are small enough for plants around their feet to retain a substantial place in the image. The title identifies an attentive activity already compatible with that distribution of space. Sutherland places observers inside the landscape rather than outside it as its sole measure. Looking becomes one of the things happening among grasses and trees.

works.title: The Mushroom Gatherers
works.credit: Jane Sutherland. The Mushroom Gatherers. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: One body bends while another remains upright, dividing the search into different moments. Cut stumps interrupt the grassy ground where their attention is directed. The task changes what counts as landscape interest: the immediate surface matters as much as a distant view. Sutherland gives an ordinary act of gathering its own bodily and spatial demands.

works.title: Blue and Gold: Portrait of Dorothy Sutherland
works.catalogueTitle: Blue and Gold: Portrait of Dorothy Sutherland
works.credit: Jane Sutherland. Blue and Gold: Portrait of Dorothy Sutherland. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Copper-coloured hair and the blue garment establish the relation announced by the title. Within it, the face is more closely defined than the clothing below. Unequal finish guides attention without requiring a rigid contour around every feature. The sitter's likeness emerges from a colour arrangement whose loosest passages remain important to the whole.

works.title: Spring
works.credit: Arthur Streeton. Spring. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Full source frame, proportional resize and JPEG compression. https://www.wikiart.org/en/arthur-streeton/spring-1890
works.description: The narrow track draws the near ground into a field where flowering trees have room to register. Fresh green and blue sky establish the seasonal contrast without filling the view with incident. Streeton allows ordinary growth to be enough. The open area around it gives relatively small changes of colour and vegetation a larger pictorial consequence.

works.title: Sydney Harbour
works.credit: Arthur Streeton. Sydney Harbour. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Full source frame, proportional resize and JPEG compression. https://www.wikiart.org/en/arthur-streeton/sydney-harbour-1907
works.description: Near branches keep the viewpoint attached to the shore, while vessels, buildings and headlands spread across the water beyond. That foreground interruption makes the harbour's breadth more apparent. Streeton balances a confined point of observation with an extensive prospect. The viewer occupies one place even when the eye can travel widely through the picture.

works.title: Winter Morning near Heidelberg
works.credit: Louis Buvelot. Winter morning near Heidelberg. Image credit: Louis Buvelot; Source credit: National Gallery of Victoria, Scan using old "Original & Fälschung"-Pictures from Hörzu 10/1988, S. 162. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Trees and their reflections form a dense central structure, opening toward brighter land behind. Buvelot uses the pool to extend the bank's dark forms rather than simply add a second view of them. Morning light must be followed through that enclosure. The picture's depth comes from a passage between masses as much as from a distant horizon.

works.title: Summer Afternoon, Templestowe
works.credit: Louis Buvelot. Summer afternoon, Templestowe. Image credit: Louis Buvelot (03 March 1814 - 30 May 1888)  (Swiss) Born in Morges, Vaud, Switzerland. Died in Melbourne, Victoria. Details on Google Art Project; Source credit: twHB-7i_mIcVaA at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Sky and dry ground share warm colours, reducing the contrast between them. A track, thin trees and fence supply enough structure to keep that continuity from becoming vague. Buvelot lets afternoon light spread across the view with few strong interruptions. The small incidents remain subordinate to the repeated conditions affecting the whole scene.

works.title: The Apple Woman and Her Husband
works.catalogueTitle: The apple woman and her husband
works.credit: Mark Gertler. The apple woman and her husband. Image credit: Mark Gertler (09 December 1891 - 23 June 1939)  (English) Born in Spitalfields, London, England. Died in Highgate, London, England. Details on Google Art Project; Source credit: 1AGFb1dEzkOQqw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The woman sits before her husband in compressed space, with apples gathered at the edge of their closely arranged bodies. Firm outlines give the pair solidity. Against those weighty forms, the red spotted scarf introduces a quicker decorative rhythm. Gertler lets a pattern enliven the group without weakening its almost crowded bodily presence.

works.title: The 28th Regiment at Quatre Bras, 1815
works.credit: Elizabeth Thompson. The 28th Regiment at Quatre Bras, 1815. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The infantry's held formation confronts the disorder of horses and figures pressing through the foreground. Smoke conceals parts of the action farther away. Thompson makes military order something maintained under visible pressure, rather than a static arrangement. The line of soldiers gives the individual dangers a collective measure, while the surrounding movement tests its apparent stability.

works.title: Interior with Figures
works.credit: Gwen John. Interior with Figures. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Pale and warmer clothing distinguish two women standing close in a dim, furnished room. Small differences of turn carry the encounter, with patterned walls and furniture leaving little spare space around them. Gwen John does not need to specify a dramatic exchange. Proximity and restrained movement already give the interior a particular human arrangement.

works.title: Untitled (Red)
works.credit: Mark Rothko. Untitled (Red). WikiArt source label: Mark Rothko Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/mark-rothko/untitled-red-1956
works.license: Mark Rothko Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: No horizon or recognisable object fixes the scale of these red and orange areas. Attention moves instead toward their soft, uneven contacts and the slight differences within colour. Rothko's boundaries remain active because they resist becoming ruled divisions. Spending time with an edge reveals change that a quick inventory of the picture's colours would miss.

works.title: Judas
works.credit: Albert Tucker. Judas. Image: WikiArt. Copyright protected (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The crouched body presses against the available space, gripping a broad wooden form above pale coins. Tucker condenses the biblical subject into a few materially forceful elements. The lowered head and cramped extremities make burden a physical relation before it becomes an ethical reading. Money remains plainly visible within the arrangement rather than being left as background information.

closingSections.title: Change the distance of your attention
paragraphs: A river bend and the edge of a red field ask for different kinds of looking. Give each the scale its argument needs, then compare what disappears when attention moves too quickly. These are collection selections, not promises of a particular hanging; confirm current access through the NGV before planning around an individual work.
